farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿سُورَةٌ أَنزَلْنَاهَا﴾ — you put al-sūra in the nominative by implying "This is a sūra which We have sent down". Do not put it in the nominative by virtue of the pronoun referring back to it, because indefinite nouns are not begun with (as mubtadaʾ, subject) before their predicates, unless that is an answer. Do you not see that you do not say "A man stood up" [rajulun qāma]; the [proper] speech is to say "There stood up a man" [qāma rajulun]. Putting the indefinite noun before its predicate is ugly because it is given a ṣila (qualifying clause) and then a predicate other than the ṣila is reported of it; so one says "A man who stands is dearer to me than a man who does not stand": it is ugly in that you are as though waiting for the predicate after the ṣila. «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 126a]» But it is good in an answer, because the speaker says "Who is in the house?" and you say "A man"; (and if you say) "A man is in it", there is no harm, because it is as though nominative by way of reply, not by way of description.
Had you put al-sūra in the accusative on the sense of your saying "We sent it down as a sūra and made it obligatory", as you say "Stripped, I beat him", it would be a valid way; but I have not seen anyone read it so.
Whoever says (فَرَضْنَاهَا) «[Translator's note: so in the source, without shadda; but the following remark on "the doubling" shows the reading meant is farraḍnāhā.]» means: We have sent down in it various obligations; or, if he wishes: We have made it obligatory upon you and upon those after you until the Day of Resurrection. The doubling (tashdīd) is good for these two senses.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلزَّانِيَةُ وَٱلزَّانِي فَٱجْلِدُواْ كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا﴾ — you put them in the nominative by what refers back to them in His saying ﴿كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا﴾. The like of this is not put in the accusative, because its interpretation is conditional (jazāʾ) (and its meaning) — and Allah knows best — is: whoever commits fornication, do that to him. Similar to it is ﴿والشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الغَاوُونَ﴾, whose meaning — and Allah knows best — is: whoever composes poetry, the misguided follow him. Likewise ﴿وَالسَّارقُ والسَّارقة﴾ and ﴿والَّلذَانِ يَأْتِيَانِهَا مِنْكُمْ فآذُوهما﴾. Had you implied before each of what we have mentioned a verb such as a command, its accusative would be permissible, and you would say: al-zāniyata wa-l-zānī fa-jlidū. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is with the yāʾ omitted, (الزانِ), like what occurs often in the Book of Allah of omitting the yāʾ from al-dāʿ, al-munād, al-muhtad and the like; it has already been explained.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَأْخُذْكُمْ﴾ — the Readers agreed on the tāʾ, except Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who read (ولا يَاخُذكم) with the yāʾ; and that is correct, as He said: ﴿وَأخَذَ الذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصيَّحْةُ﴾. In raʾfa, kaʾba and saʾma there are two forms: saʾma is faʿla, and saʾāma is like faʿāla; raʾfa and raʾāfa; kaʾba and kaʾāba. It is as though saʾma and raʾfa are the single instance, and saʾāma is the maṣdar, as you say: ḍaʾula ḍaʾālatan and qabuḥa qabāḥatan.
Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays and Mindal narrated to me from Layth, from Mujāhid, who said: al-ṭāʾifa (a party) is one and upwards. Al-Farrāʾ said: likewise Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that it is one and upwards. That [punishment] is for the two unmarried ones, not for the two muḥṣan (married). The meaning of al-raʾfa: He is saying, do not take pity on the adulteress and the adulterer and so suspend the ḥudūd (prescribed punishments) of Allah.

farraa:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلزَّانِي لاَ يَنكِحُ﴾ — it is said: the fornicator commits fornication only with a fornicatress — [this refers to] prostitutes who were in Medina. The People of the Ṣuffa thought of marrying them so as to lodge with them and partake of their food. They mentioned that to the Prophet, upon him be peace, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this; so they refrained from marrying them when ﴿وَحُرِّمَ ذٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ was revealed — He means the fornicator.

farraa:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَاتِ﴾ (also with kasra) — with fornication. ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُواْ﴾ the judges ﴿بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ فَٱجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ جَلْدَةً وَلاَ تَقْبَلُواْ لَهُمْ شَهَادَةً أَبَداً﴾ — the slanderer's testimony is not accepted; his repentance is between him and his Lord, and his testimony is discarded. Some of them used to hold that his testimony is admissible once he repents, saying: Allah accepts his repentance, and yet we do not accept his testimony!

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْوَاجَهُمْ﴾ — with fornication. It was revealed about ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī. When Allah revealed [the requirement of] the four witnesses, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of us goes in and sees a man on top of her (he means his wife), he would need to go out and bring four witnesses; by then [the man] will have satisfied his need and left. And if I kill him, I will be killed «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 126b]» for him; and if I say 'It was done with her', I will be flogged the ḥadd." Then he was afflicted with it: he went in to his wife and there was a man on top of her, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the liʿān (mutual imprecation) between them. That was because she called him a liar. The man should begin and testify, saying: "By Allah, besides whom there is no god, I am truthful in the fornication of which I have accused her"; and in the fifth: that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars in the fornication of which he has accused her. Then the woman speaks and does the same, then she stands in the fifth and says: that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful in the fornication of which he has accused her. Then they are separated and never come together again.
As for the nominative of His saying ﴿فَشَهَادَةُ أَحَدِهِمْ﴾, it is from two angles. One of them: "then it is incumbent on him that he testify", so it [the governing element] is implied, just as what makes ﴿فصيَامُ ثلاثةِ﴾ and the like nominative is implied. And if you wish, you may make its nominative due to the four testimonies: "his testimony is four testimonies", as though you said: what is required of testimony is four; as you say: "Whoever becomes Muslim, his prayers are five". Al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā used to put both the testimony and the four in the nominative; the rest of the Readers put the testimony in the nominative and the four in the accusative, because they imply for the testimony something that makes it nominative, and make it act upon the four. The accusative of the four has another explanation: that ﴿بِٱللَّهِ إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾ is made what gives the testimony its nominative [as its predicate], as you say: "My testimony is that there is no god but Allah", and "My testimony is: Allah is indeed One". Every oath is made nominative by its answer; the Arabs say: "A truthful oath: I will surely stand", and "ʿAbdallāh's testimony: you will surely stand". That is because testimony is like speech; you find it good to say: "My statement: I will surely stand", and "My statement: you are indeed standing".
And (الخامسة) in the two verses are both nominative by what follows them, namely أنّ and أنّ. Had you put them in the accusative as the object of the verb, it would be correct, as though you said: "And let him testify the fifth [time] that the curse of Allah is upon him". Likewise her action: the accusative of the fifth would be by implying "she testifies the fifth [time] that the wrath of Allah is upon her". «[Translator's note: the last sentence is garbled in the source («وكذلك فعلها يكون نصب الخامسة فإضمارِ تشهد الخامسة بأن غضبت الله عَليهَا»); translated by its apparent sense.]»

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ﴾ — its answer is left out, because its meaning is known. Likewise, whatever has a known answer, the Arabs are content to leave its answer out. Do you not see that a man insults his companion, and the insulted one says "By Allah, were it not for your father…", and it is known that he means "I would have insulted you"? The answer to such a thing is left out. He said after that, and made its answer clear: ﴿لَمَسَّكم فيِما أَفَضْتُمْ فِيهِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ ﴿ومَا زَكىَ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أحَدٍ﴾; that makes clear to you what is left out.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ كِبْرَهُ﴾ — the Readers agreed on kasra of the kāf. Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj read kubrahu with ḍamma, and that is a good form in grammar, because the Arabs say "So-and-so took on the ʿuẓm of such-and-such", meaning the greater part of it.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ﴾ — a man would meet another and say "Has such-and-such not reached you?" and mention the story of ʿĀʾisha, so that the indecency would spread. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (إذْ تَتَلَقَّونه), and ʿĀʾisha read (إذْ تَلِقُونه), which is al-walq, that is, you keep repeating it. Al-walq in travelling and al-walq in lying are alike: when one keeps on in travelling and in lying, he has walaqa. The poet said:
إن الجُلَيد زَلِق وزُمَّلقْ * جاءت به عَنْس من الشام تَلِقْ * مجوَّع البطن كِلابىّ الخُلُقْ *
(Al-Julayd is slippery and a quick one; a sturdy she-camel brought him from Syria, racing along — hungry-bellied, with the manners of the Kilāb.)
And of al-walq in the sense of lying it is said: it is al-alq and al-ilq; and the verb from it is aliqtu, and "you taʾliqūnahu". One of them recited to me:
من لىَ بالمزرَّرِ اليلامق * صَاحب إدهانٍ وَأَلْقِ آلِقِ
(Who will rid me of the one in the buttoned tunics, a man of flattery and lie upon lie?)

farraa:22-22.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَأْتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلْفَضْلِ﴾ — al-iʾtilāʾ is swearing. Some of the people of Medina read (ولا يتَالَّ أولو الفضل), which differs from the written text (al-kitāb) — from taʾallaytu. That was because Abū Bakr «[Translator's note: the source has «أبا لكرٍ», a misprint for أبا بكر.]» swore that he would not spend on Misṭaḥ ibn Uthātha and his relatives, who had spoken about ʿĀʾisha; they were people in hardship. So Allah revealed ﴿أَلاَ تُحِبُّونَ أَن يَغْفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾, and Abū Bakr said: "Yes indeed, my Lord", and restored them to his support.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ﴾ — the Readers are on the tāʾ: (يَوْم تَشْهَدُ). Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and the companions of ʿAbdallāh read (يشهد). The tāʾ is for the feminine gender of al-alsina (tongues), and the yāʾ for the masculine gender of al-lisān (tongue), and because when the verb comes first it is as though it is for one of the plural.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلْخَبِيثَاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ﴾ — evil words are for evil men; that is, that is of their doing and of what befits them. Likewise His saying ﴿وَٱلطَّيِّبَاتُ لِلطَّيِّبِينَ﴾: good words are for good men.
Then He said ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ مُبَرَّءُونَ﴾ — He means ʿĀʾisha and Ṣafwān ibn al-Muʿaṭṭal, who was slandered with her. He said ﴿مُبَرَّءُونَ﴾ [in the plural] for the two, as He said ﴿فإنْ كانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ فَلِكُلِّ واحِدً﴾ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the quotation conflates «فَإِن كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ» (4:11) with the wording of 4:12.]», meaning two brothers or more; for that reason [the mother's share] is curtailed by two. Similar to it is ﴿وكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شاهِدِينَ﴾, meaning Dāwūd and Sulaymān. Ibn ʿAbbās read (وكُنَّا لحكمهما شاهِدِينِ), which shows that they are two.

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَسْتَأْنِسُواْ﴾ — He is saying: [until] you ask permission. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās: (حتى تستأنِسُوا) — [until] you ask permission. He said: this is placed earlier and later [than its proper order]; it is only "until you greet and ask permission". They were commanded to say: "Peace be upon you; may I come in?" Al-istiʾnās in the speech of the Arabs [is as in]: "Go and look out (istaʾnis) — do you see anyone?" So the meaning here is: look to see who is in the house.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَدْخُلُواْ بُيُوتاً غَيْرَ مَسْكُونَةٍ﴾ — these are the houses that are set up for travellers: the khāns (inns) and the like.
His saying: ﴿فِيهَا مَتَاعٌ لَّكُمْ﴾ — that is, benefits for you. He is saying: you benefit from them and take shade in them from the heat and the cold. (Al-Farrāʾ said: al-fundutuq is like the khān. He said: and I heard a Bedouin of Quḍāʿa say funtuq.)

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ﴾ — the adornment is the jewelled sash and the armlet. ﴿إِلاَّ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا﴾ — such as kohl, the ring and henna dye. ﴿وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّ﴾ — He is saying: let her cover her throat and breast with a head-covering (khimār). That is because the women of the Jāhiliyya used to let their head-coverings hang down behind them, so that what was in front was exposed; so they were commanded to cover themselves. Then He said, repeating, ﴿وَلاَ يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ﴾ — He means the sash and the armlet (al-dumlūj is a dialectal form) — ﴿إِلاَّ لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوْ آبَآئِهِنَّ﴾ of kinship, up to His saying ﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُنَّ﴾.
His saying: ﴿أَوْ نِسَآئِهِنَّ﴾ — He is saying: the women of the people of their religion. He is saying: there is no harm in a Muslim woman looking at the body of a Muslim woman; but a Jewish or Christian woman should not look at her.
And it was permitted for one who has no desire for women to see that, such as the very old man, the small boy who has not reached puberty, and the impotent man. That is His saying ﴿أَوِ ٱلتَّابِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُوْلِي ٱلإِرْبَةِ﴾: the followers and hired servants. (Al-Farrāʾ said: one says irb and arab.)
His saying: ﴿لَمْ يَظْهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوْرَاتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾ — they have not reached [the age] at which they are capable with women. It is as you say: "I have mastered (ẓahartu ʿalā) the Qurʾān", that is, I have taken it in and become capable of it; and as you say of a man: "So-and-so wrestled so-and-so and ẓahara ʿalayhi", that is, he was a match for him and overcame him.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَضْرِبْنَ بِأَرْجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّ﴾ — He is saying: let her not strike one foot against the other so that the sound of the anklet is heard. That is His saying ﴿لِيُعْلَمَ مَا يُخْفِينَ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (ليعلم مَا سُرَّ من زينتهن).
As for His saying ﴿غَيْرِ أُوْلِي ٱلإِرْبَةِ﴾, it is genitive because it is a naʿt (adjective) of al-tābiʿīn, who are not specified [individuals]; therefore (غير) is fit to be a naʿt for them even though they are definite. The accusative is permissible; ʿĀṣim and others besides ʿĀṣim read it so. Similar to it is ﴿لاَ يَسْتَوِى القاعِدُونَ مِنَ المؤمِنينَ غيرُ أولى الضَرَرِ﴾. The accusative in both of them is by qaṭʿ (detachment), because (غير) is indefinite. And if you wish, you may take it as exception (istithnāʾ), so that (إلا) is put in the place of (غير), and that is sound. But the first way is better.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَنْكِحُواْ ٱلأَيَامَىٰ مِنْكُمْ﴾ — He means the free women. The ayāmā [here] are the female relatives, such as the daughter, the sister and the like. Then He said: ﴿وَٱلصَّالِحِينَ مِنْ عِبَادِكُمْ وَإِمائِكُمْ﴾ — He is saying: of your male slaves and your slave-women. Had it been (وإماءكم), referring it back to al-ṣāliḥīn, it would be permissible.
His saying: ﴿إِن يَكُونُواْ فُقَرَآءَ﴾ — is specifically for the free, men and women.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبْتَغُونَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ — He means the contract of manumission (mukātaba). (الذينَ) is in the position of the nominative, as He said ﴿وَالَّلذانِ يأتِيانِها مِنْكُمْ فآذُوهُمَا﴾; and the accusative is permissible. His saying: ﴿إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْراً﴾ — He is saying: if you expect from them fulfilment and payment of the contract. ﴿وَآتُوهُمْ مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيۤ آتَاكُمْ﴾ — He urged people to give to those under manumission contracts. Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to us from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: he gives him a third of his contract [price]; he means the master grants him a third of his contract.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُكْرِهُواْ فَتَيَاتِكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْبِغَآءِ﴾ — al-bighāʾ is fornication. The people of the Jāhiliyya used to coerce slave-women and seek earnings from them, so they would commit fornication; the people of Islam were forbidden that. ﴿وَمَن يُكْرِههُنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِن بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ﴾ — towards them [the women] — ﴿غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾.

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ آيَاتٍ مُّبَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ — Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read (مبَيِّنَاتٍ) with kasra; the people otherwise read ﴿مُبَيَّنَاتٍ﴾ with fatḥa on the yāʾ — this one and the one in the Lesser Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. Whoever says ﴿مبيَّنات﴾ makes the verb fall upon them: Allah has made them clear and plain. (And mubayyināt [with kasra] means): guiding, clear.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿كَمِشْكَاةٍ﴾ — al-mishkāt is a niche [in a wall] that does not go through. This is a parable Allah struck for the heart of the believer and the faith within it. His saying ﴿الزُّجَاجَة﴾ — the Readers agreed on ḍamma for al-zujāja; one also says zajāja and zijāja.
His saying: ﴿كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ﴾ — its first letter is given kasra and it is given a hamza. Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī narrated that to me; he said: ʿĀṣim read it so, ﴿دِرِّىء﴾ with kasra. And Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh said: ʿĀṣim read it ﴿دُرِّىءُ﴾ with ḍamma on the dāl and with hamza. It is reported of al-Aʿmash that he read ﴿دُرِّىء﴾ and ﴿دُرِّىٌّ﴾, with hamza and without hamza; both are transmitted from him. The rationale for ḍamma of its first letter together with hamza is not known: the pattern fuʿʿīl does not occur in the language except in foreign words. So the reading, if you give ḍamma to its first letter, is without the hamza; and if you give it hamza, you give kasra to its first letter. It is from your saying daraʾa al-kawkab, when a star shoots down, as though Satan were pelted with it and his skull were smashed. It is said in the exegesis that it is one of the five: Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, Venus and Mars. The Arabs call the great stars whose names they do not know al-darārī, without hamza.
Some of the Arabs say kawkab dirrī, relating it to al-durr (pearls), with kasra on its first letter and without hamza, as they said sukhrī and sikhrī, lujjī and lijjī.
His saying: ﴿تُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةٍ﴾ — (one refers it to the glass when one says (تُوقَدُ); whoever says (يُوقَدُ) refers it to the lamp. It is also read (تَوَقّدُ), in the nominative with doubling, and (تَوَقّدَ) in the accusative [i.e. as a past verb] with doubling. Whoever says (تَوَقّدُ) refers it to the glass, and whoever says (توقّد) in the accusative refers it to the lamp) — and each is correct.
His saying: ﴿شَجَرَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لاَّ شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلاَ غَرْبِيَّةٍ﴾ — it is the olive tree that grows on a rise of the land, so nothing screens it from the sun; and that is best for its oil, as has been mentioned. The eastern one is that which the sun reaches when it rises but does not reach when it sets, because it has a screen; and the western one is that which the sun reaches in the evening but not in the morning. Therefore He said: neither eastern alone nor western alone, but eastern and western «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 128a]». It is as you say in speech: "So-and-so is neither a traveller nor a resident", when he travels and stays; its meaning is that he is not solely given to staying nor to travelling.
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ﴾ — the statement breaks off here; then He starts afresh and says ﴿نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ﴾. Had it been nūran ʿalā nūrin, it would be correct, taking it [as ḥāl] from the implied nouns, the glass and the lamp.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بِٱلْغُدُوِّ وَٱلآصَالِ﴾ — the people read it with kasra on the bāʾ, and ʿĀṣim read (يُسَبَّحُ) with fatḥa on the bāʾ. Whoever says ﴿يسبَّح﴾ puts al-rijāl in the nominative by intending a renewed verb, as though He said: men glorify Him, whom neither trade distracts.
Whoever says ﴿يُسَبِّح﴾ with kasra makes it a verb of the men and implies nothing else.
As for His saying: ﴿فِي بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ ٱللَّهُ أَن تُرْفَعَ﴾, the entry of (فى) is for the mention of the lamp which He described; so He said: like a lamp in a mosque. And had you made (فى) belong to His saying ﴿يسبّح﴾, it would be permissible, as though He said: in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised, men glorify Him in them.
As for His saying ﴿أَذِنَ ٱللَّهُ أَن تُرْفَعَ﴾ — that is, to be built.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَّ تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَارَةٌ وَلاَ بَيْعٌ﴾ — trade is for those who import goods, and selling is what a man sells by his own hand; so it came in the exegesis.
His saying: ﴿تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ وَٱلأَبْصَارُ﴾ — He is saying: whoever was in doubt in his worldly life sees that clearly in the matter of his Hereafter; and whoever used to doubt, his heart increases in insight, because he did not see it in his worldly life; that is their turning about.
As for His saying ﴿وَإِقَامِ ٱلصَّلاَةِ﴾: the maṣdar of three-letter verbs [with weak middle] when you say afʿaltu — as in your saying aqamtu, ajartu and ajabtu — in all of it one says iqāmatan, ijāratan, ijābatan; the hāʾ is not dropped from it. It was brought in only because the word has lost its ʿayn [middle radical]: it should have been said aqamtuhu iqwāman and ijwāban; but when the wāw was made quiescent and after it came the alif of the ifʿāl pattern, both being quiescent, the first of them dropped; so they put the hāʾ in it, as though to augment the word. Similar to it, of what has lost part of itself and had the hāʾ put in it, is their saying: waʿadtuhu ʿidatan, wajadtu fī al-māl jidatan, and zina, diya and the like: when the wāw was dropped from its beginning, it was augmented at its end with the hāʾ. The dropping of the hāʾ in His saying ﴿وَإِقَامِ ٱلصَّلاَةِ﴾ was allowed only because they put it in annexation (iḍāfa); they said: the genitive-governing word and what it governs are like a single word, therefore they dropped it in annexation. The poet said:
إنّ الخليط أجَدّوا البين فانجرَدُوا * وأخلفُوك عِدَ الأمر الذى وَعَدوا
(The companions resolved on parting and set off in haste, and broke the promise of the matter they had promised you.)
He means ʿidat al-amr, and allowed himself to drop the hāʾ when he put it in annexation.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ كَسَرَابٍ بِقِيعَةٍ﴾ — al-qīʿa is the plural of al-qāʿ; its singular is qāʿ, as they said jār and jīra. Al-qāʿ of land is the level ground with no vegetation in it, and mirage occurs in it. The mirage (al-sarāb) is what clings to the ground, and al-āl is what appears in the forenoon like water between sky and earth.
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَهُ﴾ — He means the mirage. ﴿لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْئاً﴾ — it is a parable for the unbeliever who used to think he was upon something, and when he came before his Lord he found he had no deeds — like the mirage. ﴿وَوَجَدَ ٱللَّهَ﴾ at his deeds — He is saying: he came before Allah and He paid him his account in full.

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ كَظُلُمَاتٍ﴾ — the darknesses are a parable for the heart «[Translator's note: the source has «لقب» (title), evidently a misprint for «لقلب» (for the heart).]» of the unbeliever; that is, he does not understand and does not see, so He described his heart with darknesses. Then He said: ﴿إِذَآ أَخْرَجَ يَدَهُ لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا﴾. Some exegetes said: he does not see it — and that is the meaning — because in less than the darknesses Allah described, the onlooker cannot see his own hand. Others said: it is only a parable Allah struck; he does see it, but sees it only with difficulty, as you say "I hardly managed to reach you", when you have in fact reached. That is the [proper] Arabic sense. Some of the Arabs «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 128b]» use kāda and yakādu for certainty, treating them like ẓann (thinking) when it is used of what is certain, as in His saying ﴿وَظَنُّوا مَالَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ﴾, and in much speech.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلطَّيْرُ صَآفَّاتٍ كُلٌّ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلاَتَهُ﴾ and his glorification — you put kullun in the nominative by what refers back to it, namely the hāʾ in (صلاته وتسبيحه). If you wish, you make the knowing belong to each one, that is: each has known «[Translator's note: the source has «عاد» (returned), apparently for «علم».]» its prayer and its glorification; then, if you wish, you make the hāʾ [refer to] its own prayer and glorification, or if you wish: the glorification of Allah and the prayer which we pray to Him, and its glorification. In the first view: each — Allah has known its prayer and its glorification. Had kullan qad ʿalima come in the accusative, on [the sense of] your saying "Allah knows the prayer of each and its glorification", you would put it in the accusative because the verb falls upon what refers back to them. One of the Arabs recited to me:
كُلاًَ قَرَعنا فى الحروب صَفَاتَه * ففررتم وأطلتم الخِذلانَا
(Each of you, we struck his hard rock in the wars, and you fled and prolonged your desertion.)
But it is not permissible to say zaydan ḍarabtuhu. It is permissible with kull only because it never comes without speech before it, as though it were connected to it; as you say "I passed by the people, all of them", and "I saw the people, each saying that". Since it is an exhaustive naʿt, it is preceded by its nouns; and that is not so for Zayd or ʿAbdallāh and the like, because they are nouns that begin [the sentence].
Some grammarians have said zaydan ḍarabtuhu, putting it in the accusative by the verb as you would if there were speech before it. That is not permissible unless you intend repetition, as though he intended to make the beating fall on Zayd before it falls on the hāʾ; then, when the verb was placed later, he brought in the hāʾ by way of repetition. Similar to it, which makes it clear,
is your saying: bi-zaydin marartu bihi. And against whoever says zaydan ḍarabtuhu by itself, it can be urged that he would have to say zaydan marartu bihi; and that is nothing, because there is nothing before it that could be an extremity for the verb [to act upon].

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿يُزْجِي سَحَاباً﴾ — He drives it wherever He wills. The Arabs say: "We drive (nuzjī) the mounts", that is, we drive them along.
His saying: ﴿يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ﴾ — someone may say: bayna (between) is fit only when annexed to two or more; so how did He say ﴿ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ﴾ when it is only one? We said: it is one in form but its meaning is plural. Do you not see His saying ﴿يُنْشِئُ السَّحَابَ الثِقَالَ﴾? Do you not see that its singular is saḥāba, and when you drop the hāʾ it becomes like nakhla and nakhl, shajara and shajar? And you say: "So-and-so is between the trees (al-shajar) and between the palms (al-nakhl)"; so (بين) is fit with al-nakhl, singular as it is, because it is plural in meaning. What is not fit of this is your saying "The wealth is between Zayd": this is an error until you say "between Zayd and ʿAmr". But if by Zayd you intend the name of a tribe, it is permissible, as you say "The wealth is between Tamīm", meaning between the Banū Tamīm. Al-Ashhab ibn Rumayla said:
قفا نسألْ منازل آل ليلى * بتُوضِح بين حَوْملَ أو عُرَادا
(Halt, you two, let us ask the dwellings of Laylā's family at Tūḍiḥ, between Ḥawmal or ʿUrād.)
By Ḥawmal he meant a place that gathers [people], so (بين) was fit with it, because he meant between the people of Ḥawmal or between the people of ʿUrād.
His saying: ﴿فَتَرَى ٱلْوَدْقَ﴾ — al-wadq is rain.
His saying: ﴿فَيُصِيبُ بِهِ مَن يَشَآءُ﴾ — He punishes with it whom He wills.
His saying: ﴿مِن جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِن بَرَدٍ﴾ — the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that the mountains in the sky are of hail, created so in their make; as you say in speech: "The human being is of flesh and blood". So (من) here may be dropped and you say: "The human being is flesh and blood", and "the mountains are hail"; that is how I heard it explained. It may also be, in Arabic, [that it means] the likes of mountains and their quantities of hail, as you say "I have two houses of straw (baytāni tibnan)" — the two houses are not of straw; you only mean: I have the quantity of two houses of straw. So min in this position, when it is dropped, puts what follows it in the accusative, as He said ﴿أَوْ عَدْلُ ذَلِكَ صِيَاماً﴾ and as He said ﴿مِلءُ الأرْضِ ذهباً﴾.
His saying: ﴿يَكَادُ سَنَا بَرْقِهِ يَذْهَبُ بِٱلأَبْصَارِ﴾ — Abū Jaʿfar read it (يُذْهِبُ بالأبصارِ) «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 129a]».

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَآبَّةٍ﴾ — and (خَلَق); the companions of ʿAbdallāh read (خالق). It is reported of Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī — al-Farrāʾ said: he is the Hamdānī — that he said: I prayed beside ʿAbdallāh ibn Maʿqil and heard him say (واللّهُ خَالِقُ كلّ دابَّة). The general public otherwise read ﴿خَلَق كُلَّ﴾.
His saying: ﴿كُلَّ دَآبَّةٍ مِّن مَّآءٍ فَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَمْشِي عَلَىٰ بَطْنِهِ﴾ — it may be asked: how did He say ﴿مَّن يَمْشِي﴾, when (مَن) is only for people, and here He has used it for beasts?
I said: when He said ﴿خالق كل دابَّة﴾, people were included among them, so He referred to them with (منهم) because they are mixed with people; then He specified them with man, since He had referred to them with a pronoun proper to people. You say in speech, of a man and his riding-beast, or a man and his camel: "Who (man) are these two coming?" — you say it with man and with mā because they are mixed. Do you not see that you say "The man and his camels are coming (muqbilūn)", so that they are as though people when you say muqbilūn?

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿مُذْعِنِينَ﴾ — obedient, not compelled. One says: "He submitted (adhʿana) to my right" and "amʿana" — they are one — that is, he acknowledged it willingly.

farraa:50-50.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ يَخَافُونَ أَن يَحِيفَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ — He made injustice attributed to Allah and to His Messenger, but the meaning is only of the Messenger. Do you not see that He said ﴿وَإذَا دُعُوا إلى اللهِ ورسُولِهِ ليَحْكُمَ بَيْنهُمْ﴾ and did not say (ليحكما) [in the dual]? Allah was mentioned first only to magnify Him, as you say "What Allah wills and you will", meaning "what you will"; and as you say to your slave: "Allah has freed you, and I have freed you".

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا كَانَ قَوْلَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — this is not a report about the past, as when you say "You were only a boy"; rather it is: the saying of the believers, when they are called, ought only to be that they say "We hear". It is a moral instruction from Allah; so the exegesis has come.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ﴾ — He addresses the people directly, and its meaning is: if you (tatawallaw) turn away; so it is in the position of the jussive. Had it been about people not addressed, it would be accusative [i.e. a past verb with fatḥa], because it would be like your saying "If they stood up". In the conditional, both the forms faʿala and yafʿalu are fit, as He said ﴿فإن فَاءُوا فَإنَّ الله غَفُورٌ رَحِيم﴾.

farraa:55-55.t:
His saying: ﴿وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِنْكُمْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ لَيَسْتَخْلِفَنَّهُمْ﴾ — a promise is a statement in which both an and the answer of an oath are fit. You say: "I promised you that I would come to you", and "I promised you: I will surely come to you". Similar to it is ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَا لَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا رَأَوُا الآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ﴾; and an is fit in such speech. It has been explained elsewhere than here.
His saying: ﴿وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ﴾ — ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd and al-Aʿmash read it (وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ) with doubling, and the people read ﴿وَليُبْدِلنَّهُمْ﴾ light [without doubling]; they are close. When you say to a man "You have been changed (buddilta)", it means you have been altered and your condition has changed, without another coming in your place. So everything altered from its state is mubaddal, with doubling; mubdal, without doubling, is also permissible but is not the proper way. And when you put one thing in place of another you say "I have exchanged it (abdaltuhu)", as in your saying (abdil lī) these dirhams, that is, give me [something] in its place; and baddil is permissible. So whoever says ﴿وليُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ من بَعْدِ خوفهم أَمْناً﴾, it is as though he made the way of fear [into] security; and whoever says (وليُبدِلَنَّهُم) light, says: security is the opposite of fear, so it is as though He put security in the place of fear, that is, He took away the fear and brought the security. This is part of the breadth of Arabic. Abū al-Najm said:
* عزل الأمير للأَمير المبدَل *
(The dismissal of the emir for the emir put in his place.)
This makes both senses clear.

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾ — Ḥamza read it (لا يَحْسبنَّ) with the yāʾ here, and the position of (الذينَ) is nominative. It is rare to leave aẓunnu (I think) without acting on an or on two [objects] other than its nominative. It is as though he made ﴿مُعْجِزِينَ﴾ a noun [i.e. the first object] and made ﴿فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ a predicate for them; as you say "Let not those «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 129b; the word «الذين» is repeated in the source across the folio break.]» who disbelieve think men [to be] in your house", while they mean themselves. It is weak in Arabic. The proper way is to read it with the tāʾ, so that the verb acts on (الذينَ) and on (معجزينَ). Ḥamza likewise read in al-Anfāl (ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا سبقوا).

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿لِيَسْتَأْذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَـٰنُكُمْ﴾ — He means men and women. Then He said ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُواْ ٱلْحُلُمَ﴾ — the boys — (ثَلاَثَ مَرَّاتٍ); then He explained them, saying ﴿مِّن قَبْلِ صَـلَوٰةِ ٱلْفَجْرِ وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيَـٰبَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلظَّهِيرَةِ وَمِن بَعْدِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلْعِشَآءِ﴾ — at bedtime. Then He said (ثَلاَثُ عَوْرَاتٍ لَّكُمْ): ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash put it in the accusative, and others put it in the nominative. The nominative is dearer to me in Arabic, and that is how I read. Al-Kisāʾī reads with the accusative. [I prefer the nominative] because He had already explained them in "the times" and in what follows, so I disliked that it be repeated a third time; and I chose the nominative because the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: these qualities are the times of privacy; there is no blame on you or on them after them. So with it is an implied pronoun that puts the three in the nominative, as though you said: these are three qualities; as He said (سُورَة أنزلناها), that is, this is a sūra; and as He said ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إلاَّ سَاعَةً مِنْ نَهَارٍ بَلاَغٌ فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إلاَّ القَوْمُ الفاسِقُون﴾.
As for His saying ﴿طَوَّافُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, it too is a fresh start, as your saying in speech: "They are only your servants, and those who go about among you". Had it been accusative, it would be correct, taking it [as ḥāl] from (عَليهم), because that is definite and ﴿وطَوَّافونَ﴾ is indefinite; its accusative would be as He said ﴿مَلْعُونِينَ أيْنَمَا ثُقِفُوا﴾, which He put in the accusative because in the verse before it they are mentioned as definite, and ﴿ملعونين﴾ is indefinite.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا بَلَغَ ٱلأَطْفَالُ مِنكُمُ ٱلْحُلُمَ فَلْيَسْتَأْذِنُواْ كَمَا ٱسْتَأْذَنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ — He is saying: let them not come in upon you in these hours except with permission, nor at other than these hours except with permission. His saying ﴿كَمَا اسْتأْذَنَ الذينَ من قبلهم﴾ — He means the free [adults].

farraa:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلْقَوَاعِدُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ٱلَّلاَتِي لاَ يَرْجُونَ نِكَاحاً﴾ — they no longer aspire to marry, because of old age. ﴿فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جُنَاحٌ أَن يَضَعْنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ﴾ and ﴿من ثيابهنَّ﴾ — it is the outer cloak (ridāʾ). So the old woman was permitted to lay it aside, not intending adornment thereby. Then He said: ﴿وَأَن يَسْتَعْفِفْنَ﴾ — so that they do not lay aside the cloaks — ﴿خَيْرٌ لَّهُنَّ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (أن يضعن من ثيابهم) «[Translator's note: so in the source, with the masculine pronoun «ثيابهم».]».

farraa:61-61.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّيْسَ عَلَى ٱلأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ﴾ to the end of the verse — the Anṣār used to keep themselves from eating with the blind, the lame and the sick, saying: "We see the good food and he does not see it, so we get to it before him; the lame cannot sit comfortably so as to get what the healthy man gets; and the sick man is too weak to eat." So they used to keep them apart. Then it was revealed: there is no blame on you in eating with them. (فى) is fit in place of (على) here; you say "There is no sin on (ʿalā) maintaining ties of kinship, even if it [the kin] cuts them off", and "There is no sin in (fī) it" — it does not matter which of them you say.
Then He said ﴿وَلاَ عَلَى ٱلْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ وَلاَ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَن تَأْكُلُواْ مِن بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾ to the end of the verse. When Allah revealed ﴿لاَتَأْكُلُوا أَموالَكُمْ بينكُمْ بالباطِلِ إلاَّ أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً﴾, people gave up eating with the young and the old among those with whom, and from whose [food], Allah had permitted eating. So He said: there is no [blame] on you (in yourselves), [i.e.] in your dependants, in eating from them and with them — up to His saying (أَوْ صَدِيقِكُم), whose meaning is: or the houses of your friend. Before it is ﴿أَوْ بُيُوتِ خَالاَتِكُمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكْتُمْ مَّفَاتِحهُ﴾ — He means the houses of your slaves and their wealth; that is His saying (مفاتحه): its storehouses. The singular of al-mafātiḥ is maftaḥ when you mean the maṣdar; and when it is of the keys with which one opens — that is, al-iqlīd — it is miftaḥ and miftāḥ.
His saying: ﴿فَسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾ — when one enters upon his family, let him give greeting; and if there is no one in his house, let him say: "Peace be upon us from our Lord". When he enters the mosque he says: "Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah; peace be upon us and upon the best of Allah's righteous servants". Then He said: ﴿تَحِيَّةً مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ — that is, of the command of Allah: He commanded you to do it as a greeting from Him and as obedience to Him. Had it been nominative «[Translator's note: manuscript folio marker 130a]», on [the sense of] your saying "It is a greeting from Allah", (it would be correct).

farraa:62-62.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا كَانُواْ مَعَهُ عَلَىٰ أَمْرٍ جَامِعٍ﴾ — the hypocrites used to attend the Friday [prayer] with the Prophet ﷺ, and he would admonish them and censure them with the verses revealed about them, and they would grow weary of that; and if one of them could get up unnoticed, he would get up [and leave].

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿قَدْ يَعْلَمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَسَلَّلُونَ مِنكُمْ﴾
that is, one hides (this one behind that one). They said liwādhan «[Translator's note: the source writes «لو اذا», i.e. لِوَاذاً, the word that follows in the verse; the source does not quote it.]» only because it is the maṣdar of lāwadhtu; had it been the maṣdar of ludhtu, it would be liyādhan, that is, ludhtu liyādhan, as you say "I stood up to him qiyāman", and "your stature is a tall qiwām". His saying: ﴿لاَّ تَجْعَلُواْ دُعَآءَ ٱلرَّسُولِ بَيْنَكُمْ كَدُعَآءِ بَعْضِكُمْ بَعْضاً﴾ — He is saying: do not call him "O Muḥammad" as some of you call others; rather, honour him and say: "O Prophet of Allah, O Messenger of Allah, O Abū al-Qāsim".
